Mamatā is, according to Sāyaṇa, in one passage of the Rigveda, the wife of Ucathya and the mother of dīrghatamas. But the word may be merely an abstract noun meaning ‘selfinterest,’ a sense which it often has in the later language. Oldenberg finds a mention of Mamata (masc.) in a verse of the Rigveda as the name of a bharadvāja.
Foot notes vi. 10, 2. Cf. Mahābhārata, i. 4179 et seq.
Zeitschrift der Deutschen Morgenlāndischen Gesellschaft, 42, 212.
vi. 50, 15, where the reading of the received text is mama tasya.

Māmateya, ‘descendant of mamatā,’ is the metronymic of dīrghatamas in the Rigveda and the aitareya brāhmaṇa.
Foot notes i. 147, 3; 152, 6; 158, 6.
viii. 23, 1; śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka, ii. 17. For mamatā, cf. Bṛhaddevatā, iii. 56; iv. 11.
